tools.name: deposit
tools.description: Shields your own funds: wallet public balance -> its private (shielded) balance. Use when the user says deposit/shield. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. No Hinkal fee, only gas. For someone else's private balance use deposit_for_other.

tools.name: withdraw

When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Fee is on top: the private balance must cover amount + fee.

tools.name: deposit_for_other

When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. No Hinkal fee, only gas. Recipient must be the public address of a registered Hinkal wallet. For your own balance use deposit.

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

recipient.description: Recipient's public address; must belong to a registered Hinkal wallet so its private address can be resolved

tools.name: private_transfer
tools.description: Your private (shielded) balance -> another Hinkal user's private balance, with no public trace of sender, recipient, or amount. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Fee is on top: the balance must cover amount + fee. Recipient must be the public address of a registered Hinkal wallet; for an arbitrary address use private_send or withdraw.

chainId.description: Chain id. Supported: 1 (Ethereum), 8453 (Base), 137 (Polygon), 42161 (Arbitrum), 56 (BNB Chain), 5042 (Arc), 5042002 (Arc Testnet), 4217 (Tempo), 4663 (Robinhood), 501 (Solana), 728126428 (Tron), 3448148188 (Tron Nile), 728126428 (Tron), 501 (Solana)

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

recipient.description: Public address of a registered Hinkal wallet; the transfer lands in its private (shielded) balance

tools.name: private_swap
tools.description: Swaps one token for another INSIDE your private (shielded) balance - no public trace of the trade. Use when the user says swap/trade/convert privately or the funds are already shielded. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Aggregator-routed at the best rate; fee comes out of the swap output; returns receivedAmount. Pass toChainId to BRIDGE privately instead (EVM chains only, same token symbol on both); on success it returns the source tx hash plus the expected destination amount. A bridge that ERRORS may still have moved the funds - they land in a temporary wallet, so check balances and run recover_temporary_wallet_funds before telling the user nothing happened. For a public swap from the wallet balance use wallet_swap.

chainId.description: Chain id. Supported: 1 (Ethereum), 8453 (Base), 137 (Polygon), 42161 (Arbitrum), 56 (BNB Chain), 5042 (Arc), 5042002 (Arc Testnet), 4217 (Tempo), 4663 (Robinhood), 501 (Solana), 728126428 (Tron), 3448148188 (Tron Nile), 728126428 (Tron), 501 (Solana)

fromToken.description: Token to swap FROM (sell): symbol (e.g. "USDC") or on-chain address

toToken.description: Token to swap TO (buy): symbol (e.g. "ETH") or on-chain address; must differ from the from-token

amount.description: Token amount in human decimal units (e.g. "1.5" tokens), NOT wei/base units

toChainId.description: Optional destination chain id: set to a DIFFERENT chain to BRIDGE privately instead of swapping. Supported between these chains only (1 (Ethereum), 8453 (Base), 137 (Polygon), 42161 (Arbitrum), 56 (BNB Chain), 5042 (Arc), 4217 (Tempo), 4663 (Robinhood), 501 (Solana), 728126428 (Tron)) and only for the same token symbol on both chains (toToken resolves on this chain). The bridge fee is charged ON TOP of the amount, so the shielded balance must cover amount + fee - leave headroom rather than bridging the whole balance. Small amounts work but lose a larger share to the fee. Omit for a same-chain swap

slippagePercentage.description: Optional max slippage in percent (0-10), e.g. 1 = 1%. Defaults to 0.7 when omitted

tools.name: recover_stuck_funds
tools.description: Withdraws stuck UTXOs of one token to a public address. Use only after get_stuck_balances reports stuck funds. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Returns one transaction hash per recovered UTXO batch.

chainId.description: Chain id. Supported: 1 (Ethereum), 8453 (Base), 137 (Polygon), 42161 (Arbitrum), 56 (BNB Chain), 5042 (Arc), 5042002 (Arc Testnet), 4217 (Tempo), 4663 (Robinhood), 501 (Solana), 728126428 (Tron), 3448148188 (Tron Nile), 728126428 (Tron), 501 (Solana)

tokenAddress.description: Token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC", "ETH") or on-chain address (EVM 0x, Solana mint, Tron T.../0x). Pass the symbol directly for common tokens; only call list_tokens if a symbol fails to resolve.

toAddress.description: Public address that receives the recovered tokens

tools.name: recover_temporary_wallet_funds
tools.description: Recovers funds stranded in temporary in-transit wallets by an interrupted or failed private swap/bridge. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Destination is automatic - shielded balance or public wallet, per the original flow - and the fee comes out of the recovered amount. Omit chainId to scan all EVM bridge chains. Returns recovered, failed, and skipped entries.

chainId.description: Optional chain id to limit the sweep to one chain (1 (Ethereum), 8453 (Base), 137 (Polygon), 42161 (Arbitrum), 56 (BNB Chain), 5042 (Arc), 4217 (Tempo), 4663 (Robinhood)). Omit to scan every EVM bridge chain

tools.name: private_send
tools.description: Unlinkable payout: your wallet public balance -> one or more public addresses, with no on-chain link between sender and recipients. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. One transaction per recipient, each returning a txHash and a scheduleId; payouts complete asynchronously - poll check_private_send_status per scheduleId. Recipients receive the full amount; the fee is charged on top.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Checks the Hinkal API is up. Use it to distinguish a real outage from a bad-request error when another tool fails. No account required.

tools.name: get_contract_addresses
tools.description: Deployed Hinkal contract addresses keyed by chain id for every supported chain: hinkalAddress, plus hinkalHelperAddress where deployed. Tron addresses are in 0x hex form; on Solana hinkalAddress is the Hinkal program id. On EVM and Tron it is the contract a token allowance must be granted to before deposit. No account required.

tools.name: get_enclave_public_key
tools.description: Current public key of the Hinkal enclave, used to encrypt payloads to it. Pair with get_enclave_attestation, which reports the verificationPublicKey the attestation vouches for. No account required.

tools.name: get_enclave_attestation
tools.description: Use when the user wants to verify the enclave. Returns the attestation proving the Hinkal API runs in a genuine secure enclave: jwt (signed, covers your nonce), imageDigest (running image), verificationPublicKey (key it vouches for). This server has already verified Google signed the jwt, that it covers this nonce and key, and that it attests Hinkal's own enclave service account running a hardened image with debug disabled - the call errors instead of returning if any check fails. No account required.

nonce.description: Caller-generated nonce echoed inside the attestation document, proving it was produced for this request rather than replayed. Use a fresh random value each time, 8 to 88 characters.

tools.name: get_wallet_addresses
tools.description: Returns the public EVM, Tron, and Solana addresses of your Hinkal wallet. This is the address to FUND before a deposit (token + native gas).

tools.name: export_wallet_key
tools.description: Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to export or back up the wallet. SENSITIVE: reveals the private access key (full wallet control) plus restore instructions; it appears in this conversation, so warn the user and get explicit confirmation before calling it. Never call it on your own initiative.

tools.name: initiate_x402_request
tools.description: Step 1 for any URL that may require payment: user shares a paid API or paywalled link, wants to buy/unlock content, or a request came back 402. Calls the URL WITHOUT paying, so it is always safe to try. paymentRequired false -> the resource answered without asking for payment; report its status and body as-is (a 404 or 500 lands here too, and is an error, not free content). paymentRequired true -> offers[] with tokenSymbol, human amount, chainId, payTo, and supported. Quote the price in plain words ("0.001 USDC on Base") and get the user's agreement, then pay that amount via complete_x402_request. Offers with supported false cannot be paid - say which chain or scheme they need rather than retrying. The user provides only the URL - never ask them for schemes, chain ids, or tool names.

url.description: Full http(s) URL of the (possibly x402-gated) resource

body.description: Optional raw request body. A JSON body is sent with Content-Type application/json unless headers override it

headers.description: Optional extra request headers (e.g. an API key). Payment headers are added automatically

tools.name: complete_x402_request
tools.description: Step 2: pays a 402-gated URL and returns its content. Moves real funds irreversibly. When token, amount, chain, and recipient are all stated, execute immediately; ask only if a required detail is missing or ambiguous. Here the price the user approved IS the required detail: set maxAmount to it, from an explicit approval or a budget they already gave. Never invent a cap - if no price was agreed, quote one first with initiate_x402_request. A resource demanding more than maxAmount is refused with nothing withdrawn, signed, or paid. source "private" (default): unshields the exact amount to a fresh temporary wallet that signs the payment, so the seller cannot link it to the user - Hinkal fee on top, and the unshield takes up to a few minutes. source "public": signs from the public wallet balance - cheaper and immediate, no privacy. x402 v1/v2, "exact" scheme, EVM chains only. Report the content first, then amount paid and the settlement explorerUrl. If it fails after the unshield the funds sit on the temporary wallet - run recover_x402_temp_wallets.

url.description: Full http(s) URL of the (possibly x402-gated) resource

body.description: Optional raw request body. A JSON body is sent with Content-Type application/json unless headers override it

headers.description: Optional extra request headers (e.g. an API key). Payment headers are added automatically

maxAmount.description: User-approved spending cap in human decimal units of the payment token (e.g. "0.10" USDC). Payment happens only when the required amount is at or below this cap; otherwise nothing is signed or paid

chainId.description: Optional chain id to pick when the resource offers payment on several chains. x402 payments are EVM-only: 1 (Ethereum), 8453 (Base), 137 (Polygon), 42161 (Arbitrum), 56 (BNB Chain), 5042 (Arc), 5042002 (Arc Testnet), 4217 (Tempo), 4663 (Robinhood)

source.description: "private" (default): pay from the shielded balance via a fresh temporary wallet, unlinkable to the user's wallet, Hinkal fee on top. "public": pay from the public wallet balance, cheaper/faster, publicly linked

tools.name: recover_x402_temp_wallets
tools.description: Recovers funds stranded by a failed private x402 payment: sweeps every temporary payment wallet that still holds tokens back to your main wallet. Run when complete_x402_request failed after the withdrawal, or anytime to check for leftovers - it only moves what it finds. No inputs; it checks the temporary wallets this machine recorded, on whichever chains they were created. The temporary wallets need no gas; the main wallet pays gas on each affected chain. instructions:
WALLET ON THIS SERVER:
- Set up AUTOMATICALLY on first use and kept across restarts. Never ask the user for a wallet address or chain to "connect" - just call the tool you need.
- Every transaction is signed and broadcast SERVER-SIDE by Hinkal; there is nothing for you to sign.
- The wallet starts EMPTY. Before the first deposit, call get_wallet_addresses and tell the user to fund the address for their chain (token + native gas).

Hinkal moves tokens between the wallet's PUBLIC balance and its PRIVATE (shielded) Hinkal balance on each supported chain. Amounts are human decimal units (e.g. "1.5"), never wei.

Keep to the fewest steps: confirm token, amount, chain, and recipient, then call the one tool with the token SYMBOL (e.g. "USDC"), amount, and chainId. Chain ids are standard (1 = Ethereum, 137 = Polygon). Do NOT preflight with list_tokens, list_chains, get_balances, or get_public_balances - tools accept symbols, and a spend self-reports any missing balance, gas, or allowance. Use those lookups only when a call fails or the user asks for balances.

Choosing the fund-moving tool (each runs server-side and returns a txHash):
- shield own funds -> deposit; fund someone ELSE privately -> deposit_for_other
- pay from shielded balance, fully private -> private_transfer (recipient must be a registered Hinkal wallet)
- unlinkable payout to any public address(es) -> private_send
- unshield to a public address -> withdraw
- what a withdraw / private_transfer / private_send / private_swap / private bridge will cost -> estimate_fee (read-only, nothing is sent); use it when the user asks about fees or sets a fee limit, then let them decide
- swap tokens inside the shielded balance -> private_swap; plain public swap from the wallet balance -> wallet_swap; either one bridges to another chain when given toChainId (a private bridge reports the source tx hash and the expected destination amount on success; if it errors the funds may still have moved, so check balances and recover_temporary_wallet_funds before reporting it as a no-op)
- wallet_send and other wallet_* tools are plain PUBLIC actions, no privacy - only when the user explicitly wants that.
- funds stranded by an interrupted private swap/bridge -> recover_temporary_wallet_funds (sweeps the temporary in-transit wallets; omit chainId to scan every EVM bridge chain)
Insufficient balance or gas returns a clear error naming what is missing, so never preflight balances before a spend.- wallet_send and other wallet_* tools are plain PUBLIC actions, no privacy - only when the user asks.
- fetch a PAID URL / paid API / 402 paywall -> initiate_x402_request for the price quote (free), then, once the user agrees or already stated a budget ("pay up to $0.05"), complete_x402_request with maxAmount = that approved amount. User supplies only URL + budget. Private by default (unlinkable temporary wallet); source "public" = cheaper, no privacy. Report content first, then amount paid + settlement explorer link. If a private x402 payment fails after the withdrawal, recover_x402_temp_wallets sweeps the stranded funds back to the wallet.

Reporting a result: show the FULL txHash and any scheduleId (never truncate), and render an explorerUrl as a markdown [View on explorer](url) on its own line. After a spend, report the txHash and expected balance directly - do not call get_balances to verify unless asked (it re-scans and is slow).
